issues.issue: Whether the principal claimant's detentions and political problems in Iran are credible, so as to give a well-founded fear (family group and political opinion, s.96)
issues.applicant_position: Principal claimant was detained, interrogated and harassed in Iran for anti-regime views and 2009 demonstrations, and fears persecution.
issues.result_quote: the claimants do not have a well-founded fear of persecution by reason of an absence of credibility with respect to principal aspects of their narrative

issues.issue: Whether the claimants' delay in claiming refugee protection after arriving in Canada undermines their subjective fear
issues.applicant_position: Principal claimant still hoped to return to Iran, so the claim was delayed about three months.
issues.result_quote: indicates that when they left Iran they did not have a fear of persecution

issues.issue: Whether the wife faces persecution in Iran as a member of the Sufi sect of Shia Islam (religion, s.96)
issues.applicant_position: Wife does not feel secure practising her Sufi faith openly in Iran.
issues.result_quote: there is no reasonable chance or serious possibility that she would be persecuted by reason of her religious beliefs

issues.issue: Whether the claimants would be persecuted on return to Iran for having claimed refugee protection in Canada
issues.applicant_position: Authorities would learn of the Canadian claims and persecute them on return, relying on country documents.
issues.result_quote: there is no cogent evidence that the claimants would be subjected to persecution by reason of having filed claims for refuge protection in Canada

issues.issue: Whether the claimants face a personal risk to life or of cruel and unusual treatment on return to Iran (s.97)
issues.applicant_position: Would face risk to life or cruel treatment on return to Iran.
issues.result_quote: there is no risk that the claimants would be subject personally to a risk to their lives or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment
